_provenance: measurements: published literature values, carried verbatim with their arXiv identifiers. arbitration: closed-form toy defined in this file. h_convention: parsed from the pipeline's constants.py.

measurements.label: Planck 2018
measurements.note: Not a distance measurement at all: an inference of H0 from the acoustic scale of the last-scattering surface, under an assumed cosmological model.

measurements.label: SH0ES 2022
measurements.method: Cepheid-calibrated Type Ia supernova distance ladder
measurements.note: A ladder: geometric parallaxes calibrate Cepheids, Cepheids calibrate supernovae, supernovae reach the Hubble flow. Every rung is calibrated on the rung below it.

measurements.label: CCHP 2019 (TRGB)
measurements.note: A third method that swapped one rung of the ladder and landed between the two anchors, with a systematic term twice its statistical one. It did not arbitrate.

measurements.label: H0LiCOW 2020
measurements.note: Quoted at 2.4% — under an assumed family of lens mass profiles.

measurements.label: TDCOSMO IV 2020
measurements.method: the same technique with the lens mass profile left free
measurements.note: Same systems, one modelling assumption relaxed: the uncertainty went from ~2% to ~8%. The extra 6% was always there; it was in the assumption, not in the data.

measurements.label: GW170817
measurements.method: one bright standard siren (GW + electromagnetic counterpart)
measurements.note: The first siren H0: distance from general relativity, redshift from the host galaxy's spectrum. Published as 70.0 +12.0 −8.0 — the scale of a single-event measurement.

measurements.label: GWTC-3 dark sirens
measurements.method: galaxy-catalogue redshifts, with the GW170817 counterpart
measurements.note: The state of the art in this book's own genre: no counterpart, the redshift information taken from a galaxy catalogue. This is the published dark-siren analysis combined with GW170817's counterpart; the catalogue events on their own constrain far more weakly. Not a like-for-like 'before/after' against the 2017 counterpart-only row above -- that is a different analysis of different data.

arbitration.ceiling_branch_note: parked on the early-universe anchor the far anchor is the late one (the wider sigma), which is the more DEMANDING of the two placements; parked on the late-universe anchor the far anchor is the tighter early one and the cap relaxes
